headline: Money leaving the AI trade drove Indian IT stocks to their best week in about 18 years, with Nifty IT up 11.72 percent while the Nasdaq fell 4.48 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 fell 1.09 percent to 7,659.44 and the Nasdaq 2.15 percent to 26,140.03 on Friday, while the Dow lost only 0.34 percent and still gained 0.67 percent for the week as money moved into banks and defensives. The cause named across coverage was the financing of AI capital spending rather than chip demand, with a 10 year yield of 5.098 percent and WTI above 101 dollars pushing the semiconductor ETF to an eighth straight losing session and knocking more than 260 billion dollars off a basket of 45 software companies.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed at 23,146.15, up 0.65 percent on Friday and 2.78 percent on the week, and Bank Nifty added 0.06 percent, with Nifty IT up 3.92 percent on TCS, Tech Mahindra and Wipro results as global investors rotated into laggards. Foreign institutions bought 1,166 crore rupees of cash equities after selling 5,285 crore the day before while domestic institutions sold 3,661 crore, the rupee ended at 94.96, and on Saturday HDFC Bank posted profit up about 4.7 percent and ICICI Bank up about 20.1 percent.
summary.global: The Nikkei rose 1.39 percent to 65,324.29 after TSMC reported a sixth consecutive record quarter with net profit up about 69 percent, the Hang Seng added 0.52 percent, and the FTSE 100 and DAX gained 0.38 and 0.95 percent on lighter technology weightings. Brent settled 3.72 percent higher at 109.86 dollars on an 8.6 million barrel US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk, which lifted BP and Shell ADRs to 52 week highs, while gold held 4,181.10 dollars, silver closed a week down 6.06 percent and bitcoin sat at 81,333.51.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.
